data.one_liner: Embed VoIP audio and video calls based on SIP and RTP protocols into Flutter apps.
data.what_it_does: Provides native SIP client implementations for multiple platforms with a unified API. Allows managing multiple SIP accounts, making audio/video calls, call transfers, conferencing, echo cancellation, push notifications, and text messaging.
use_when: You need to integrate SIP-based VoIP audio and video calls into a Flutter app.
You require built-in CallKit, PushKit, or FCM support for incoming calls on mobile platforms.
avoid_when: You are building a generic audio/video streaming or recording app that does not use the SIP protocol.
You want a fully open-source Dart WebRTC implementation without native proprietary vendor SDKs.
strengths: Cross-platform support for Android, iOS, MacOS, Windows, and Linux with a unified API.
Ready-to-use models and UI helpers for fast integration.
Embedded support for Apple CallKit/PushKit and Android FCM.
weaknesses: Trial mode limits call duration to 60 seconds unless a paid license is purchased.
Depends on proprietary native binaries and external SIP PBX services.
data.setup_notes: Requires adding the dependency, configuring native push notification services (CallKit/PushKit for iOS, FCM for Android), and optionally supplying a commercial license key for production use.
